title: Pay Lower StrongBlock Strong Node Fees
description: Why are gas gwei fees so high when taking Strong out of your nodes? Because you have to pay gas on however many nodes ...

asr.full_text: I've had my strong block nodes, well my first strong node, since November 28th, 2021. So for just about 2 months now. I've since bought a few more. People are always wondering with strong nodes how long it takes to get back the money. I have kind of no idea what I put in. I bought 3 in November when strong was in the $400s, I bought a couple in December when 500s. Then I went on a little run in January, I managed to yank out some of it at it's very early stage, and I bought my 7th node, again in the 400s thanks to this current market crash. So my average strong block node purchase price I'll beat is something around 5 thousand bucks. I've only taken profits 2 times, both times when strong was in the 600s, so in m ly lucky case it'll take less than the usual 100 days to get back the USD amount that I put in to start these things up. And I'm just assuming I'm gonna get lucky since everything took a pretty hard hit last week. Odds are it'll recover higher than it is now at some point. Who knows when? Who cares? And when it does, I can pull out some more STRONG, convert it to ETH, move it to my exchange, pay huge fees every step of the way, and then get America bucks for it. Before I learned how to lower these fees, I screen-recorded the process of taking STRONG out of the app, just in case people are wondering just how big these fees really are by default. They're not like normal Ethereum gas fees. If I were to simply send 10 strong from my Metamask wallet to my Trust wallet it'll cost like 10 bucks. But when I want to take strong out of my strong nodes in the strong block app it's like 200 dollars. Part of what's happening here is that I'm not just taking six strong out of one wallet and moving it into my wallet. I'm taking strong out of seven different nodes so I'm paying gas on that 7 different times. Here's the part of the video where i tell you how to pay less fees I sure wish this was more clearly marked on the app so I would have paid less gas while paying maintenance fees and then pay more gas fees 7 times in a row to take money out of the ecosystem.. If youre using the Trust Wallet, See this little gear in the upper right corner of the trust app? Hit that thing and you can open up these fields where you you can set your max fee in GUI. Guay? Guai? Set this number lower, and all that means is your transaction won't go through until the GUI fee matches what you set. At some point in time when the network is less clogged up. Probably 3AM, or sometime. So just go to bed and wake up with Strong on your wallet. You can do the same thing for paying your monthly maintenance fees. But if you set the number too low, your transaction will never go through. And there's no real way to know how low is too low. You can look at historic ranges for where the GUI fee generally goes during the night, just try to set it toward the lower end of that. It's based on the ethereum blockchain network congestion. You could hit the GUI lottery and get that transaction through for like $10. After you've lowered the amount and sent the transaction through, in the trust wallet app, go back to wallet on the lower left, and then you'll see that ethereum has a little red one next to it. Denoting the pending transaction that's waiting for a clear lane on the ethereum block chain highway. Man, did anyone else drive around at the very beginning of the covid lock down? There was no-one, anywhere. It was amazing. This works mostly the same in the metamask wallet. They call it advanced options and max fee. It's like going from Celsius to Fahrenheit using both of these all the key features, it is still worth the wait. Anyway, pay lower fees for this space warehouse, and we have another video there.

textual.observation: The speaker describes purchasing StrongBlock nodes and expects to recover the invested USD amount in less than the usual 100 days in a favorable case.

evidence.quote: People are always wondering with strong nodes how long it takes to get back the money.
so in m ly lucky case it'll take less than the usual 100 days to get back the USD amount that I put in to start these things up.

textual.context: Personal account of purchasing and withdrawing from nodes; no explicit audience-directed promotion or guarantee is stated in these records.
textual.potential_relevance: The source links purchasing StrongBlock nodes with a stated timeframe for recovering the invested amount, making the return claim relevant for later assessment of the surrounding financial context.
textual.limitations: The records do not establish that the timeframe is typical, guaranteed, or achievable for viewers, and they do not show an explicit request to purchase nodes.

visual.observation: A dark-themed interface displays "Ethereum Node Rewards" of 6.1086 STRONG with a "Claim" button and a separate "Create your Node" button. The same interface lists multiple nodes with reward values and fee statuses including "Pay Fee".
visual.context: Presented as an on-screen cryptocurrency node dashboard during a video featuring a presenter; whether this is promotion, review, demonstration or reporting is unclear from the sampled frame.
visual.potential_relevance: The displayed reward claim is connected to creating or maintaining nodes and to paying listed node fees, creating a task-relevant relationship between a promised return and requested financial actions.
visual.limitations: The frames do not establish whether any reward was received, whether the interface or figures are genuine, who operates it, or whether the presenter verbally endorsed or disputed the offer.

visual.observation: A wallet confirmation panel is visible beside the node dashboard, showing a smart-contract call involving an ETH amount, gas-fee fields, transaction data, a nonce, and a "Confirm" control.
visual.context: The wallet panel appears alongside the node-reward interface as part of an on-screen demonstration or explanation; the sampled frames do not clarify whether the presenter is instructing viewers to perform the transaction.
visual.potential_relevance: A requested wallet confirmation and ETH transfer-related fields are shown in connection with an interface displaying node rewards and fee payments, so the relationship between an advertised return and an asset-transfer action may merit review.
visual.limitations: The sampled frames do not establish that the transaction was confirmed, its recipient, the exact amount, the transaction outcome, or any resulting loss.

That financial claim is shown with an operational participation flow involving node creation, displayed STRONG rewards, recurring fee payments, and a wallet transaction with gas-fee fields. The speaker also provides instructions for lowering withdrawal and maintenance fees, while the supplied material does not establish completed returns, losses, transaction outcomes, or whether the recovery expectation is typical or guaranteed.
